Two posts left the set the same day: 'statistical_learning_theory_dependent_data.qmd' and 'minimum_description_length.qmd' were here only for an unclosed ':::' opener, and blog 25cf42e5c5 fixed the asymmetric fences that produced it -- zero corpus-wide, so it is the synthetic 'segmenter_conformance.qmd' that keeps the construct (D69).
scoring: 3 * (distinct protected kinds) + sum(min(count, 10) per kind) + 10 * sum(log2(1757 / posts_with_feature)) over 22 edge-case features. The set is a greedy set cover of the 22, not the top N by score.
content: Every fixture is an EXCERPT, not a copy. The blog source is private and this repo is public, so a post's frontmatter and prose may not live here: each file is cut to the construct its `hard_case_for` names plus enough surrounding prose to segment, its frontmatter reduced to `title`, and its HTML comments replaced by ones written here (F17). `source` names the post the construct was found in, not a file this repo reproduces.

posts.hard_case_for: Top of the ranking (score 463.8): the only fixture with HTML comments, and it carries mid-line $$ math, $$..$$ {#eq-} attributes so it is where the stylebot and livingthing configurations disagree most.

W2's runaway fence: a fence span ran 999 chars past its own closer and swallowed three .callout-tip divs. Also nested divs and a four-backtick fence, and the interaction is the bug, so the excerpt keeps the callouts and the fences that swallowed them together.

The construct the first twelve missed and the sweep caught: a '`````{verbatim}' fence quoting a shorter '```{r}' one. Under the pre-D69 closer the inner ' ``` ' closed the outer fence and the outer's own '`````' line re-opened, running 1,525 chars into the prose. Live in 2 posts corpus-wide; this fixture is where the fast path pins the fix.
W4's unclosed fence at EOF (since fixed in the blog); still the plain-fence fixture, with fences that quote fences and mid-line math.
W2's four-backtick Quarto include -- and the include sits inside a callout div, so the fence span merges into the div's. The excerpt keeps the include inside its div for that reason.
A raw <script>/<style> block (3 posts corpus-wide), plus '  # comment' lines inside an indented fence that ATX_HEADING_RE reads as headings.
The second raw-HTML-block instance, in a different shape from python_cli's.
Indented fences (8 posts corpus-wide) whose bodies contain indented '#' comment lines -- the fence reading must win over the heading reading.
A blockquote glued to the prose beneath it (31 posts) -- the blockquote span must stop at the quote, not run on into the paragraph.
The only '{#tbl-...}' layout div in the corpus, and the only div class in the set that is neither .callout-*, #fig- nor #refs.

The corpus's ONLY indented ':::' div -- a fig div inside a list item at two spaces of indent. The source post is 'draft: true', so only the three markup lines are reproduced; the prose around them is placeholder text written here.
